key_insight: For liver lesions ≤40 mm, dLI-RADS achieved 80% internal lesion-level accuracy versus 74% for LI-RADS, meeting the study’s non-inferiority criterion (p = 0.04).
clinical_relevance: Interpretable AI could support more consistent assessment of small liver lesions on multiphase CT for early hepatocellular carcinoma detection.
method: Analyzes manually segmented liver lesions on multiphase CT.
Combines neural network predictions with quantitative measurements reflecting LI-RADS major imaging features.
Uses logistic regression to estimate hepatocellular carcinoma probability.
evidence_signal: This multicenter retrospective study used histology for hepatocellular carcinoma and a composite reference for other lesions, with internal accuracy assessed using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests.
watch_item: Manual segmentation may limit workflow scalability, and the supplied abstract does not report external-test performance results.
paper_title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
